searchText: L2Beat is impressively on the ball for their risk assessment page. Right now L2s are all centralized in some way (except Fuel, which was just a prototype and isn't maintained). I mean if the end goal is to optimize execution, block producing / sequencing of transactions being relatively centralized is an inevitability no? So the key to a robust system would be DA + a broad base of nodes verifying proofs + easy exit mechanisms (and I guess robust cryptoeconomics for optimistic designs) in case of sequencer downtime But yes L2beat is an excellent resource. Also wtf is metis… you can decentralise the sequencer and still achieve highly performant sequencing. Question on EIP-4844 + L2: In the FAQ vitalik mentions optimistic rollup fraud proofs will need to use the entire content of a relevant blob as calldata. At 125 kb/blob we're looking at up to 2 million gas in calldata. Is it just agreed upon that fraud proofs are gonna be extremely expensive? What about when full danksharding rolls out and x16's blob sizes?
